incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186-2194 (partnership) and 2236-2245 (limited partnership / societe en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), arts. 9, 21, 27, 31-33; Canada Income Tax Act partnership pass-through rules (T5013 / Quebec Releve 15)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Direction de l'immatriculation et de la publicite legale, clicREQ portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration d'immatriculation (registration statement) filed electronically through clicREQ, supported by the notarized acte de societe en commandite and the REQ name-search certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; the partnership agreement must determine each partner's contributions (art. 2238 CCQ). Contributions of limited partners must be capital (cash or property) and fully documented to preserve the liability shield; no escrow account is statutorily mandated, but the general partner must open a dedicated bank account and satisfy PCMLTFA/KYC client identification rules before accepting contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the capital contributions and subscriptions of the initial limited partners, as set out in the acte de societe en commandite, are hereby accepted and deemed fully subscribed. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the limited partnership is fixed at [address of the establishment], Quebec, and is designated as the siege social. RESOLVED, that the general partner appoints [name] as its manager and [name] as authorized representative (fonde de pouvoir) for all filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency, and for opening the partnership bank account. RESOLVED, that all necessary municipal and environmental licensing steps are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation (demande de recherche de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - clicREQ enterprise-name search module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the REQ name search on clicREQ with up to three proposed names. The selected name must include the mandatory legal element 'societe en commandite' / 'S.E.C.' or 'limited partnership' / 'L.P.' and must not conflict with registered enterprise names, trademarks, or misleading/descriptive terms. The system issues a name-search certificate valid for 90 days and reserves the name for the limited partnership.
required_dossiers: REQ name-search / name-reservation request
Up to three proposed names with distinctive element
Brief activity statement (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 - manufacture of games and gaming accessories)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, REQ issues a notice of refusal identifying the conflicting element. File a revised name-search request with a new distinctive element or submit written representations within 30 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarized limited partnership agreement (acte de societe en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Chambre des notaires du Quebec (CNQ) - civil-law notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign an authentic notarial deed organizing the societe en commandite. The deed must identify the general partner (associe commandite), who administers the partnership under CCQ arts. 2239-2241, and the limited partners (commanditaires), and must state the capital contributions, profit-sharing rules, the registered office address in Quebec, and the appointment of the general partner's statutory representative. A limited partner may not perform external management acts and may not contribute services, preserving the liability shield.
required_dossiers: Valid photo identification (passport or Quebec driver's licence) of each partner
Proof of address and, for corporate general partners, an excerpt from the enterprise register
Proposed capital contribution schedule and funding source declaration
Draft limited partnership agreement with named registered office
Notarization instructions and fee estimate from the CNQ notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests complementary evidence or corrections, amend the draft deed and sign a rectificatory minute; no adverse state sanction applies at this contractual stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - clicREQ electronic filing; simultaneous issuance of the NEQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaration d'immatriculation within 60 days of the creation of the partnership obligation (P-44.1, art. 27). Insert the exact name, the Quebec head office address, the principal activity (NAICS 339930), identification of the general partner, and confirmation of the registered office. Pay the CAD 50 registration fee online; REQ issues the NEQ certificate of immatriculation and publishes the notice in the enterprise register.
required_dossiers: Notarized acte de societe en commandite (PDF extract)
REQ name-search certificate / reservation receipt
Identifiers and addresses of the general partner
Declaration of the establishment address in Quebec
Authorization of the filing person (fonde de pouvoir) if not the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a demande de renseignements complementaires or rejects the filing, submit the requested original documents and pay the amendment fee for a declaration modificative; unresolved refusals may be appealed to the Registraire under P-44.1, arts. 45-47.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax account registration with Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec (QST, TP-1015 payroll) and Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST, payroll) - Business Registration Online (BRO) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the NEQ is issued, register the limited partnership with the CRA for GST/HST and with Revenu Quebec for QST using the NEQ. The CRA BRO single-window session imports the Quebec enterprise data and Revenu Quebec assigns the QST number. Also register an employer payroll account if the partnership will hire staff, and complete the anti-money-laundering client identification file for the bank mandate.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate of immatriculation
Date and place of the notarized partnership deed
Partnership address and contact details
Schedule of expected GST/HST and QST registration (activity 339930)
Direct deposit authorization and general partner's authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Quebec questions the partnership taxation year-end or the legal name, cure by supplying the REQ extract and a copy of the notarial deed; use Represent a Client / Mon dossier d'entreprise for corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business permit, zoning clearance and fire safety inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permits and inspections department of the host city (e.g., Ville de Montreal - Service des permis d'exploitation; other cities under the Cities and Towns Act, CQLR c C-19)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal application for a commercial/industrial operating permit (permis d'exploitation), including a site plan demonstrating that epoxy resin casting, solvent (acetone) storage and finished dice inventory fall within permitted industrial zoning. Attach the fire-safety and evacuation plan, a certificate of lease or ownership, and the CNESST notice of commencement of activities. The municipal inspector confirms compliance with the fire code for Class IB flammable liquids and issues the permit before production begins.
required_dossiers: Municipal permit application form
Site plan, floor plan and lease/title proof
Material Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for epoxy resin, hardener and acetone
Fire-safety and evacuation plan approved by the municipal fire service
CNESST registration acknowledgment and prevention program
REQ certificate of immatriculation and GST/QST numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On refusal, remedy by amending plans (e.g., ventilation and storage cabinets), applying for a minor zoning derogation from the municipal zoning committee, or appealing the permit decision to the municipal council within the statutory appeal delay; MELCCFP authorization may be required if hazardous material storage exceeds 100 kg/L.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal permits and inspections service under the Cities and Towns Act (CQLR c C-19) for industrial occupation; Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE) for investment and industrial support; no sector-specific federal or provincial manufacturing licence applies to ISIC 3240 tabletop gaming accessories
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation d'etablissement commercial/industriel (municipal commercial-industrial operating permit) - Manufacture of epoxy resin role-playing dice

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction des autorisations environnementales; municipal delegated certification under the Environment Quality Act (LQE, CQLR c Q-2)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - artisan-scale epoxy casting is excluded from the full environmental impact assessment and review procedure (REIE, CQLR c Q-2, r. 9) at proposed production scale; an individual certificate of authorization under LQE art. 22 or an activity declaration under art. 31.0.5 is required if volatile organic compound (VOC) releases or hazardous residual materials exceed regulatory thresholds; storage above 100 kg/L of hazardous materials triggers a MELCCFP authorization under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (RMD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC and solvent vapour (acetone) releases from casting must comply with the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1) concentration thresholds, odour nuisance prohibition and best available technique requirements; wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must meet municipal pH limits of 5.5-9.5 with no free resin, hardener or acetone content; hazardous waste (uncured epoxy, contaminated acetone, wiping material) must be accumulated and eliminated under the RMD; workplace air exposure limits under the Quebec RSST apply including acetone TWAEV of 500 ppm.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the municipal fire department under the Fire Safety Act and the National Fire Code, limiting Class IB flammable liquids (acetone) to approved safety cabinets with spark-proof electrical equipment; structural load inspection for casting and grinding work benches; CNESST workplace registration with a health and safety prevention program and SDS training before operations; finished sharp-edge polyhedral dice must be packaged with adult-use safety labelling and must not be marketed as children's toys under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST registration, federal Business Number (BN) and federal tax administration; Revenu Québec – Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial tax filings; Registraire des entreprises du Québec – prior mandatory provincial enterprise registration (NEQ), with the CRA Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec business portals used for account setup.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the Limited Partnership with Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). 2) Register through CRA Business Registration Online to obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number and open a GST/HST account program (RC1). 3) Apply separately to Revenu Québec for a QST account unless an eligible partner is elected as the partnership registrant for both taxes. 4) Non-resident partners carrying on business through a Quebec establishment must appoint a valid representative for service of process; tax accounts must be active before any taxable supply is made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists for Canadian partnerships; income, gains, losses and QST input tax refunds flow through to partners for federal and Quebec income tax purposes. Relevant elections include: (i) partnership GST/HST registrant election under subsection 273(1) of the Excise Tax Act and the parallel Quebec QST partnership election; (ii) partnership non-calendar fiscal period election under subsection 249.1(4) of the Income Tax Act; and (iii) limited transitional elections on the formation or acquisition of a partnership. Canada applies OECD hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.4 and 18.5 of the Income Tax Act rather than an elective hybrid mismatch regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal Goods and Services Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) – a two-tier VAT-style system applied separately by CRA and Revenu Québec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or across the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); non-resident persons soliciting business in Canada may be required to register regardless of turnover. The QST small supplier threshold is aligned at CAD 30,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose mandatory e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transaction reporting, or digital stamping. Peppol-based e-invoicing is voluntary. Registered suppliers must issue commercial invoices containing prescribed GST/HST/QST information and retain them for at least six years. Revenu Québec may require electronic transmission of invoice data during an audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST and QST registrant may zero-rate handmade epoxy resin RPG dice (tangible personal property) when the goods are physically exported from Canada by the supplier, delivered to a common carrier for export, or sent by mail/courier to a foreign destination, provided the supplier possesses documented proof of export within the required period. Zero-rated exports allow full input tax credits (ITCs) and QST input tax refunds (ITRs) without charging GST/QST. Canada generally does not impose a fixed statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is used for export substantiation and financing documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A where required)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Carrier certificate or courier shipment proof
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank remittance or payment proceeds record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec can deny zero-rating, reassess GST/QST, and charge interest plus civil penalties where export documentation is incomplete or inaccurate. Knowing false statements may trigger a 50% civil penalty (e.g., Excise Tax Act subsection 285(1)), criminal fines of CAD 25,000 to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment (Excise Tax Act subsection 289(1)), and parallel QST penalties. The ordinary reassessment window may be extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation, and fraudulent export zero-rating claims remain subject to retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central bank), Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (prudential regulation), Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (AML/FT reporting), and Quebec's Autorité des marchés financiers (securities/registration requirements for underlying investment solicitation, if any).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency under the Currency Act. No exchange control approval or licensing is required for current or capital account transactions. Partnership capital contributions, profit distributions, royalty payments, and management fees may be remitted cross-border freely, subject only to income tax withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and any applicable tax treaty (e.g., Canada–US Treaty). Dividend and interest withholding rates are typically reduced for treaty residents; no separate profit-remittance permit exists. Transfer pricing requirements apply to related-party cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Foreign currency receipts may be retained, deposited in foreign currency accounts, or converted at market rates without regulatory approval. No statutory timeline applies to remitting export earnings into the domestic banking system.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Offshore digital EMI licences (e.g., UK FCA EMI) are not recognised as bank licences in Canada. Such entities cannot accept deposits or provide intra-Canada clearing without registration as a money service business (MSB) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and registration with FINTRAC. Wallet-based fintech platforms (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury) operate only as payment intermediary systems with fund-safeguarding limitations. They are viable as secondary disbursement and crowdfunding payout rails, but the primary corporate treasury, capital escrow, and FX clearing functions must reside with a Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted in Quebec for non-resident and Canadian directors, provided that identity verification is completed using FINTRAC-compliant methods (e.g., notarised certified true copies of passports, live video verification, and verification of corporate registration through a Quebec registry search). Individual banks may, at their discretion, require one signing director with Canadian residency or a physical visit, but OSFI and FINTRAC do not mandate in-person appearance. For dual-purpose escrow/operational structures, banks may request a Quebec-registered office address and a board resolution authorising the specific account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound crowdfunding (Kickstarter) proceeds without prior declared business history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crowdfunding campaign platform export, pledge level summary, production timeline, supplier quotes, product prototype photos, list of non-refundable obligations, and a written business plan describing fulfilment and refund policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal as a business clearing account receiving retail funding from global backers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PayPal business account verification, transaction history for the past six months, refund and dispute resolution policy, anti-fraud chargeback rationale, and details of physical manufacturing location in Quebec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners contributing large capital sums
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports, evidence of source of funds (three months bank statements), partnership agreement with capital contribution schedule, legal opinion on foreign investment restrictions (if any), and no immediate redemption language.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purchase of epoxy resin, polymer chemicals and sharp-edge casting equipment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), supplier invoices, commercial purchase contracts, proof of compliance with WHMIS/Quebec occupational health and safety regulations, and confirmation that resin is not a Scheduled precursor chemical.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected remittances to overseas contract manufacturers for dice polishing or liquid-core components
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturing services agreement, invoice referencing specific import order numbers, customs broker documentation (B3/CBSA), proof that the manufacturer is not a sanctioned party, and bank commentary on recurring volume.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are executed via high-value SWIFT MT103 messages to the Quebec-domiciled operating account. The remitter must use the following narrative: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – [LP NAME] – QC REGISTRATION NO. [NEQ]'. For USD-participating LPs, use a US correspondent bank path through the Canadian bank's USD account at a US clearing institution. All inbound wires greater than CAD 10,000 are reportable as electronic fund transfers to FINTRAC. The bank must code the purpose economically as 'Contribution to partnership equity'; no exchange control permit is required. For payments routed through PayPal, remittances are received as a PayPal batch settlement to the Canadian bank account, and the underlying donor name must be shared with the bank if requested for source-of-funds verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for raw materials and contract manufacturing are cleared using SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) for amounts above CAD 25,000, and ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System) or Lynx batch EFT for domestic payments. For international contract manufacturing of custom liquid-core dice components, the preferred rail is an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) with a 60-day sight tenor and the presentation documents restricted to the commercial invoice, packing list, and transport document. PayPal is used exclusively for refunds, micro-purchases, and crowdfunding reward fulfilment under CAD 1,000. All USD outflows are converted to CAD via the bank's spot market, with FX quoted under the bank's operational hedging framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD outright forward contracts with a Schedule I bank (plain vanilla, using ISDA + CSA or bank proprietary master agreement for corporates)
CAD/USD European-style vanilla currency options (cash-settled or physically settled)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) for long-term balance-sheet hedging of capital contributions and profit distributions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-convertible emerging-market currency pairs; CAD/USD NDFs are not recommended due to full convertibility and deep onshore liquidity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Legal Publicity Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for the Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the LP's registration date (e.g., if registered on June 15, file by August 14 annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of C$7 per month up to C$35; three consecutive years of non-filing triggers administrative dissolution (radiation) by REQ.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (including financial schedule and partner allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal period due date: 5 months after the LP's fiscal year-end (March 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: C$25 per month per partner (minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500 for a single return); gross negligence or willful omission can lead to additional civil penalties and criminal prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a Quebec limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A audit may be triggered by the partnership agreement, a lender covenant, or if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under securities law (not ordinary for a tabletop RPG dice manufacturing LP).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS if the partnership is publicly accountable; CRA requires the partnership's books to be maintained under Canadian tax accounting rules for T5013 reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the LP must report in its annual declaration every 'particular having ultimate control' (personne ayant le contrôle ultime). Any change in ownership or control, including transfers of limited partnership interests, must be filed with REQ within 60 days of the change and confirmed annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of general partners (names, addresses, contributions)
Register of limited partners (interest held, contributions, withdrawals)
Minute book containing partner resolutions and capital calls

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
